identity: Writer and women's rights activist · People's Republic of China · 1875–1907
title: Qiu Jin's birth chart
metaDescription: Qiu Jin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.4° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Fixed signs carry eight of the nine placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. The fixed signs hold what the cardinal signs start; a chart weighted there finishes its sentences.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Scorpio, but precisely: 15.4°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Jupiter in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Libra (29.4°), Venus in Scorpio (27.1°), Mars in Aquarius (10.3°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste tuned to mood and undertow, drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Saturn directly across the wheel from Uranus, 0.3° off exact. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach. Behind it, Mercury opposition Neptune at 1.9°, and the Sun conjunction Jupiter at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Saturn opposes Uranus while both square the Sun. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Venus in Scorpio at 27.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aquarius at 19.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 water, 3 air, 2 earth, 1 fire by element and 8 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde. Mercury changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.1° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
